products.name: Cisco Webex AI
products.note: Meeting intelligence; real-time translation; noise removal; enterprise security

reading.body:
Cisco frames itself as an infrastructure provider for AI workloads, not an AI product company, emphasizing networking, silicon, and data center modernization as the substrate on which AI runs.

This positioning matters because it identifies a critical dependency in AI scaling that sits upstream of the model-makers themselves. As training and inference demand grows, the networking hardware and software that moves data between compute nodes and data centers becomes a bottleneck. Cisco's emphasis on "AI-optimized networking" and "purpose-built programmable silicon for hyperscalers" reflects this reality. The company is not competing to build better models or interfaces. It is competing to be the plumbing that allows the builders to scale.

The one consumer-facing product listed, Cisco Webex AI, is an exception that proves the rule. It sits in a different category, meeting intelligence rather than infrastructure. The gap between this and the rest of Cisco's portfolio suggests the company sees its core defensibility in layers below the application. Whether that positioning holds depends on whether networking and silicon remain differentiable as AI infrastructure centralizes and the major cloud providers build more of these capabilities in-house.

The data does not cover Cisco's actual revenue split between infrastructure and applications, its market share in any of these categories, or the technical performance of its silicon and networking products against competitors. It reflects how Cisco describes itself, not independently verified capability or adoption.

profile_text.body:
Cisco is a worldwide technology leader founded in 1984 and headquartered in San Jose. The company describes itself as powering an inclusive future through AI infrastructure, secure networking, and software solutions. According to its website, Cisco offers AI-optimized networking that unifies scale, speed, and resilience for AI workloads, purpose-built programmable silicon for networks across hyperscalers and enterprises, and security embedded at every layer of the network. The company also highlights data center modernization to support traditional and AI workloads.

Cisco's AI product offering includes Cisco Webex AI, which provides meeting intelligence, real-time translation, noise removal, and enterprise security capabilities. Beyond Webex, the company positions itself around autonomous operations with policy-bound agents that execute complex workflows, and Cisco IQ, described as a unified AI-powered experience delivering real-time insights, automation, and agent-driven guidance for Cisco support and professional services. The company notes that the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team relies on Cisco networking and security for AI workloads processing race data.

Cisco is a public company trading under ticker CSCO with CIK 0000858877.
